evidence: AURKA overexpressed in enzalutamide-resistant CRPC (Beltran 2011, Mosquera 2013)
concern: Tozasertib (VX-680/MK-0457) development discontinued by Merck 2007 due to QTc prolongation
alternative: Alisertib (MLN8237) — selective AURKA inhibitor, Phase II in CRPC exists
verdict: BIOLOGY CORRECT but lead drug has safety issues. Alisertib is better candidate.

published_validation.preclinical: Liadi & Odero-Marah AACR 2023: enza + alisertib in LNCaP-HMGA2
published_validation.phase_II_single_agent: Beltran et al. CCR 2019: alisertib in NEPC, exceptional responders with AURKA/N-myc
published_validation.intercepta_addition: RNA velocity identifies NE-like trajectory at diagnosis for patient selection

evidence: MAPK activation in CRPC lineage plasticity (Bluemn 2017)
concern: BRAF mutations rare in prostate (~1%). Dabrafenib works in BRAF-mutant tumors.
alternative: MEK inhibitors (trametinib) may be more relevant — target downstream of BRAF
verdict: BIOLOGY PLAUSIBLE but BRAF may not be the right node. MEK inhibitor combo more rational.

evidence: PARP + CHK1 synthetic lethality published (Booth 2013, Sen 2017)
concern: AZD7762 had cardiac toxicity in trials. Prexasertib (LY2606368) is current CHK1 inhibitor.
verdict: BIOLOGY VERY STRONG. Need better CHK1 inhibitor than AZD7762.
